Consider the test class `TestEnumDeserializeExceptions` in `marshmallow_qa/fields_deserialize_m5_exceptions/files/testcase.py`, run with `pytest marshmallow_qa/fields_deserialize_m5_exceptions/files/testcase.py::TestEnumDeserializeExceptions` (all of its test methods, aggregated together). Focus on the method `marshmallow.fields.Enum._deserialize` defined in `src/marshmallow/fields.py` (the `_deserialize` method of class `Enum`; NOT any other field class's `_deserialize`). Across ALL invocations of that method during ALL test methods of the class, count how many times each exception type is observed in the `Enum._deserialize` frame.

Observation rule: an exception is observed in the frame when it is raised by code executing in that exact frame (e.g. a `raise` statement in the method body), OR when it propagates into that frame out of a callee (e.g. an exception escaping a call made on one of the method's lines). Each such event counts once per frame invocation per exception: an exception that propagates into the frame and is then caught by an `except` clause in the frame counts once; an exception that propagates in and is not caught (so it continues to propagate out of the method) also counts exactly once (leaving the frame does not count again). A new exception raised inside an `except` handler is a separate observation of its own type (in addition to the one that was caught). Exceptions raised AND fully handled inside a callee (never escaping the callee into the `Enum._deserialize` frame) do NOT count. Exceptions in other frames (callers such as `List._deserialize`, `Schema` methods, or the test itself) do NOT count. Counts are totals over all invocations and all test methods: the same type observed in five different invocations contributes five.

Naming: use bare `type(exc).__name__` for built-in exception classes (e.g. `ZeroDivisionError`, never `builtins.ZeroDivisionError`), and `module.QualName` (i.e. `f"{type(exc).__module__}.{type(exc).__qualname__}"`, e.g. `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError`) for every non-built-in exception class.

Answer format: a JSON object with a single key `exception_type_counts`, whose value is a list of objects `{"count": <int>, "exception_type": <str>}`, one per exception type observed at least once (types never observed are omitted; no entry has count 0). Sort the list by `exception_type` ascending (plain Python string ordering, case-sensitive); since each type appears exactly once, there are no ties.
